intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy traditional sakura mochi and bento boxes, and soak in the festive atmosphere with locals and families. The illuminated evening viewing is especially breathtaking.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Walk the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional craft stalls and street food vendors. Kids will love trying ningyo-yaki (doll-shaped cakes) and watching artisans at work. A perfect blend of history and family fun.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and educational experience for families, this UNESCO World Heritage site tells the story of the 1945 atomic bombing through powerful exhibits and preserved ruins. The Peace Park surrounding the museum offers reflective walks along the river and the iconic Atomic Bomb Dome. Essential for understanding modern Japanese history.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Tenryu-ji Garden
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic natural and cultural landscapes. Combine the visit with the UNESCO-listed Tenryu-ji Zen garden featuring stunning cherry blossom trees reflected in its central pond. Rent a rickshaw for a family-friendly tour of the surrounding historic village.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japanese culinary culture at the world-famous Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), wagyu beef skewers, and matcha-flavored treats from dozens of stalls. Join a guided family-friendly food tour to learn about Japanese food traditions, seasonal ingredients, and the art of sushi-making from local vendors.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing and clearing customs, take the airport limousine bus or train to your hotel (Aegean Bliss Resort, beachfront area). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the nearby beachfront promenade to get your bearings. Enjoy the coastal scenery and late cherry blossom views if trees are still blooming.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate neighborhood around the hotel. Visit a nearby convenience store (7-Eleven, FamilyMart, or Lawson) to pick up budget-friendly snacks and essentials. Take a short evening walk along the beach to unwind after your long flight.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or grab a quick bite at the airport (airport food courts offer ramen or udon sets for ¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Convenience store dinner (onigiri, sandwiches, hot foods, and drinks) — budget ¥600–¥1,000 per person. Great introduction to Japanese convenience store culture!

day_by_day.notes: Purchase an IC card (Suica or Pasmo) at the airport for seamless train and bus travel throughout the trip. Consider buying a data SIM or pocket Wi-Fi. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag is real after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the nearest local shrine or temple in the area for a peaceful morning cultural experience. Many Japanese shrines are free to enter and offer beautiful cherry blossom-lined pathways in April. Participate in the 'omikuji' fortune-telling tradition (¥100–¥200).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby local park or castle ruin known for cherry blossoms (hanami). Bring a picnic mat and snacks from the convenience store for a budget-friendly hanami (flower-viewing) picnic under the sakura trees — a beloved Japanese tradition perfect for families.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a local shotengai (covered shopping arcade) for affordable souvenirs and street food. Try yakitori skewers, taiyaki (fish-shaped pastry), or takoyaki (octopus balls) from street stalls.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or grab onigiri and green tea from a convenience store (¥300–¥500)
meals.lunch: Picnic under the cherry blossoms — convenience store bento boxes, onigiri, and drinks (¥800–¥1,200 per person)
meals.dinner: Local ramen shop near the hotel — a hearty bowl of ramen costs ¥700–¥1,000. Look for restaurants with plastic food displays or picture menus.

day_by_day.notes: April is peak cherry blossom season — parks and shrines will be beautifully decorated. Arrive at popular spots early to avoid crowds. Bring a light jacket as April evenings can be cool near the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the nearest historic city or town (e.g., Kyoto, Nara, Kamakura, or Hiroshima depending on hotel location). Take an early local train or highway bus (book in advance for cheapest fares). Visit a UNESCO World Heritage Site such as a famous temple complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the historic city. Visit a free or low-cost museum or historical district. In Nara, feed the famous free-roaming deer in Nara Park (deer crackers ¥200). In Kyoto, walk the Philosopher's Path lined with cherry trees at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by early evening. Relax and rest after a full day of sightseeing.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store onigiri and coffee (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Soba or udon noodle shop in the historic city (¥600–¥900). Look for standing noodle bars (tachigui) for the cheapest options.
meals.dinner: Gyudon (beef rice bowl) chain restaurant such as Yoshinoya or Sukiya near the train station (¥400–¥700 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Research train schedules the night before. Use Hyperdia or Google Maps for train route planning. A day trip return ticket on local trains is usually ¥1,000–¥3,000 depending on distance. IC card works on most local trains.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local fish market or morning market near the beachfront hotel. Many coastal Japanese towns have early morning markets where you can watch the day's catch being sold and sample fresh seafood. Arrive by 8:00–9:00 AM for the best experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby historical museum or cultural center (entry ¥200–¥500). Learn about the region's local history and traditions. Many Japanese museums offer free entry for children under 15, making this very family-friendly.
day_by_day.evening: Try a local sento (public bathhouse) experience — a quintessential Japanese cultural tradition. Entry typically costs ¥400–¥500 per person. Bring your own towel or rent one for a small fee.

meals.breakfast: Fresh seafood breakfast at the morning market — grilled fish sets or fresh sashimi rice bowls (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) restaurant — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person for a satisfying family lunch
meals.dinner: Supermarket dinner — visit a local supermarket after 6:00 PM when bento boxes and sushi are discounted by 30–50%. Budget ¥500–¥800 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The sento experience is a wonderful family activity and cultural immersion. Note that tattoos may not be permitted in some sento establishments. Children usually enjoy the warm baths. Bring a small bag with toiletries.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a nearby traditional Japanese garden. Many prefectural or municipal gardens charge minimal entry fees (¥150–¥400) and are stunning in April with cherry blossoms and spring flowers in full bloom. Bring a camera for memorable family photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local craft or pottery workshop where families can try hands-on traditional Japanese crafts such as origami, furoshiki wrapping, or pottery making. Community centers often offer these at low cost (¥500–¥1,500 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free outdoor event or festival if available (April is rich with spring festivals — matsuri). Check local tourist information boards or the hotel reception for upcoming events. Evening cherry blossom illuminations (yozakura) are magical and usually free.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store (¥300–¥600)
meals.lunch: Teishoku (set meal) at a family restaurant such as Denny's Japan or Gusto (¥700–¥1,000 per person, free drink bar included)
meals.dinner: Okonomiyaki (savory pancake) restaurant — a fun, interactive family dinner where you cook at the table. Budget ¥800–¥1,200 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check the local tourist information office (kanko annai-jo) — usually located near train stations — for free maps, discount coupons, and event listings. Staff often speak basic English.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby castle town. Japan's castles (such as Himeji, Matsuyama, or Kumamoto) are iconic historical landmarks. Many offer discounted family entry rates. Explore the castle grounds and enjoy panoramic views from the top floors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the castle town's samurai district or historic merchant streets (many are free to stroll). Visit small local shops for affordable regional souvenirs and snacks. Try local regional specialties sold by street vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel and enjoy a relaxed evening. Visit a nearby izakaya (Japanese pub) for an affordable dinner with a wide variety of small dishes to share as a family. Many izakayas are family-friendly early in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast on the go (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Castle town local specialty — try regional dishes sold near the castle such as castella cake, regional soba, or local rice dishes (¥600–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner — order edamame, karaage (fried chicken), yakitori, and rice. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person including soft drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Many castles offer free entry to children. Check the official castle website for hours and entry fees before visiting. Some castles require climbing steep stairs — wear comfortable shoes. April weather can be unpredictable; carry a compact umbrella.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning near the hotel — enjoy the coastal scenery, collect shells, and take family photos. Japan's beachfront areas in April are uncrowded and peaceful. Some beaches near resort areas have small aquariums or marine life exhibits nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local aquarium or science museum (great for families with children). Japanese aquariums are world-class and entry is typically ¥1,000–¥2,000 per adult, less for children. Spend 2–3 hours exploring.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the beach promenade. Stop at a seaside snack stall for soft-serve ice cream or fresh seafood skewers. Enjoy the relaxed coastal atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — Japanese bakeries (pan-ya) offer delicious melon pan, curry bread, and cream-filled rolls for ¥100–¥200 each
meals.lunch: Seafood rice bowl (kaisendon) at a local seafood restaurant near the coast (¥1,000–¥1,500) — a splurge-worthy mid-trip treat
meals.dinner: Supermarket discounted bento or convenience store hot foods (¥500–¥800) — a rest-day budget dinner

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally relaxed — a mid-trip rest day to recharge. Avoid over-scheduling to prevent travel fatigue, especially for families with children. Use the afternoon aquarium visit as a fun, educational activity.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a famous Shinto shrine complex in the region. Participate in the purification ritual at the temizuya (water basin), make a small offering at the main hall (¥5 coin is traditional), and explore the grounds. Many shrines have beautiful torii gate pathways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby traditional crafts village or open-air folk museum (minka-en). These outdoor museums preserve traditional Japanese farmhouses and demonstrate historical rural life. Entry is usually ¥300–¥600 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Cook your own dinner using ingredients from a local supermarket — buy pre-marinated meats, fresh vegetables, and rice. Many hotels have common kitchen areas or kitchenettes. Alternatively, try a shabu-shabu or sukiyaki restaurant on a budget set menu (¥1,500–¥2,000 per person).

meals.breakfast: Convenience store tamago sando (egg sandwich) and canned coffee — a classic Japanese morning combo (¥350–¥500)
meals.lunch: Soba noodle restaurant near the shrine — cold or hot soba sets with tempura (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Supermarket self-cook dinner or budget shabu-shabu set (¥1,000–¥2,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: When visiting shrines and temples, follow etiquette: bow before entering torii gates, don't point at sacred objects, and keep voices low. Dress modestly. Many shrines sell beautiful omamori (good luck charms) for ¥500–¥1,000 — lovely affordable souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final major day trip — visit a nearby famous cherry blossom spot or scenic nature area for last hanami photos. Consider a river cruise or scenic boat ride if available in the area (¥500–¥1,500 per person). Capture final sakura memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping at a local market or 100-yen shop (Daiso or Can★Do). Stock up on affordable Japanese gifts: matcha Kit Kats, local snacks, stationery, and small crafts. Budget ¥2,000–¥5,000 for souvenirs depending on your list.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at a slightly nicer restaurant — try a tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) restaurant or a local specialty restaurant. Celebrate the end of a wonderful trip with a memorable meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (last full hotel breakfast — enjoy it!)
meals.lunch: Onigiri and snacks from the 100-yen shop or convenience store while shopping (¥400–¥600)
meals.dinner: Tonkatsu set meal at a dedicated tonkatsu restaurant — includes miso soup, rice, and cabbage salad (¥1,200–¥1,800 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully tonight to avoid morning rush. Vacuum compression bags are useful for saving luggage space. Check airline baggage allowances — Japan Post also offers affordable parcel shipping (takkyubin) if you've bought too much!

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of the hotel. If time permits before departure, take one last walk along the beachfront and enjoy a final convenience store breakfast or nearby café. Visit any last spots within walking distance of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to the airport. Allow plenty of time — aim to arrive at least 2–3 hours before your flight. Use IC card for train or take the airport bus. Return IC card at the airport for a refund of the remaining balance (minus a ¥220 handling fee).
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Browse duty-free shops at the airport for last-minute gifts. Japanese airports (especially major international ones) have excellent food courts — enjoy a final ramen or sushi meal before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — final Japanese breakfast (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Airport food court — ramen, udon, or sushi set (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining before departure

day_by_day.notes: Return your IC card (Suica/Pasmo) at the airport's JR service center for a refund. Keep all receipts for tax refund claims — Japan offers 8% consumption tax refunds on purchases over ¥5,000 at participating stores. Present your passport at the store's tax-free counter before leaving Japan.

trip_options.title: Classic Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy traditional sakura mochi and bento boxes, and soak in the festive atmosphere with locals and families. The illuminated evening viewing is especially breathtaking.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-in — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Allow time for immigration, baggage claim, and airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 1.5–2 hours depending on location).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a gentle orientation stroll around the immediate beachfront neighborhood to get your bearings. Visit a nearby convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) to pick up snacks and essentials — a quintessential Japanese experience in itself.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first dinner close to the hotel to recover from jet lag. Explore the local dining street or resort area for a casual izakaya (Japanese pub-style restaurant) dinner. Order yakitori skewers, edamame, and miso soup to ease into Japanese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or skip — arrival is at 13:00
meals.lunch: Airport ramen or soba noodle shop inside the terminal before or after customs — budget ¥900–¥1,400
meals.dinner: Local izakaya near the resort — order a set meal (teishoku) with grilled fish, rice, miso soup, and pickles — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Jet lag from Europe (LH = Lufthansa, likely from Germany/Europe) will be significant — Japan is UTC+9. Prioritize rest. Set alarms for an early start on Day 2 to reset your body clock. Purchase a Suica/Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless train travel throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street — Head to Asakusa early (by 8:00–8:30 AM) before the crowds arrive. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon Thunder Gate, stroll the 250-meter Nakamise shopping arcade lined with traditional souvenirs and snacks, and explore the main temple hall. Light an incense stick and draw an omikuji (fortune paper) for a hands-on cultural experience. The five-story pagoda and surrounding Nakamise stalls are perfect for family photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Senso-ji, walk 10 minutes to the Sumida River waterfront to admire the Tokyo Skytree. Take a short Sumida River cruise (Tokyo Cruise Water Bus) from Asakusa to Hamarikyu Gardens — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a teahouse on a tidal pond, perfect for hanami if cherry blossoms are still lingering in mid-April.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Asakusa for dinner in the vibrant restaurant district. Explore Hoppy Street (Hoppy-dori) for casual yakitori and cold draft beer in an old-Tokyo shitamachi atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) with morning set — toast, egg, and coffee for ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Tempura teishoku set lunch at Daikokuya Tempura in Asakusa, a historic restaurant open since 1887 — budget ¥1,500–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Hoppy Street izakaya in Asakusa — grilled skewers, oden, and local draft beer — budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. Hamarikyu Gardens admission is ¥300 per adult. The Sumida River cruise costs approximately ¥1,000 per person. Wear comfortable walking shoes — expect 8–10 km of walking today. Mid-April cherry blossoms may still be partially visible in Tokyo depending on the year.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Arrive at Tsukiji Outer Market by 8:00 AM for the freshest experience. The Outer Market (free to enter and still fully operational) is a paradise for food lovers. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, tuna sashimi, and matcha soft-serve ice cream. Wander the narrow lanes packed with seafood vendors, knife shops, and tea merchants. This is one of Japan's most authentic culinary cultural experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Harajuku and Omotesando. Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine — a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji, offering a peaceful contrast to the busy market morning. Afterward, stroll the wide, tree-lined Omotesando boulevard (Tokyo's Champs-Élysées) for window shopping and architecture appreciation.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the famous Shibuya Crossing scramble experience — one of the busiest pedestrian intersections in the world. Watch the crossing from the Starbucks or Mag's Park observation deck, then explore the surrounding entertainment district.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market grazing breakfast — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and grilled items — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 (this IS the experience)
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepes on Takeshita Street or a casual ramen shop near Omotesando — budget ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Shibuya restaurant — try a shabu-shabu (hot pot) set meal at a mid-range chain like Nabezo or MoMo Paradise — budget ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest on weekday mornings but Saturday is still excellent. Meiji Jingu is free to enter. Keep an eye on your belongings at Tsukiji — the lanes are narrow and busy. The Shibuya Crossing is most dramatic at dusk and evening when all the neon signs are lit.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — Take the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa Station (approximately 2 hours, ¥1,360 one-way or purchase a Tobu Nikko All Area Pass for better value). Nikko is a UNESCO World Heritage mountain town famous for its ornate Tosho-gu Shrine complex, dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu, founder of the Edo shogunate. The shrine complex features the famous 'See no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil' three monkeys carving and the Sleeping Cat (Nemuri-neko). Explore the main shrine buildings in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's shrine and temple complex, including Rinnoji Temple and the Futarasan Shrine. If energy allows, walk the cedar-lined avenue (Sugi Namiki) — a stunning 35-km avenue of ancient cryptomeria cedars, parts of which are walkable near the shrine area. The mountain setting with rivers and waterfalls is spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by late afternoon/early evening (last convenient trains depart around 17:00–18:00). Quiet dinner near the hotel to rest after a full day of travel and walking.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or onigiri and green tea from a convenience store before catching the train
meals.lunch: Nikko yuba (tofu skin) cuisine — a local specialty — at a restaurant near the shrine complex such as Gyoshintei or Hippari Dako — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Neighborhood soba or udon restaurant near the hotel — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Tosho-gu Shrine admission is ¥1,300 per adult, ¥450 for children. The Tobu All Area Pass (¥4,780 from Asakusa) includes round-trip train fare and unlimited bus rides in Nikko — excellent value for families. Wear layers as Nikko is mountainous and cooler than Tokyo in April. Start early to maximize time.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Tokyo to Kyoto via Shinkansen — Take the Tokaido Shinkansen Nozomi or Hikari from Tokyo Station (approximately 2 hours 15 minutes to Kyoto). Book seats in advance. Enjoy the iconic view of Mount Fuji from the right side of the train (seats A/B) approximately 40–45 minutes after departure from Tokyo. Arrive in Kyoto mid-morning and check into your Kyoto accommodation (or store luggage at the station if check-in is not yet available).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cherry Blossom Viewing at Maruyama Park — Head directly to Maruyama Park in the Higashiyama district. This is Kyoto's most beloved hanami (flower-viewing) spot, centered around the magnificent 80-year-old weeping cherry tree (shidare-zakura). Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy bento boxes from a nearby convenience store or market, and soak in the magical atmosphere. Mid-April may catch late-blooming varieties even if somei yoshino has peaked. Explore adjacent Yasaka Shrine.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the atmospheric Higashiyama walking path — the stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes lined with traditional machiya townhouses, craft shops, and tea houses. This is quintessential old Kyoto. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple for a stunning illuminated evening view (check if spring illumination is running in April).

meals.breakfast: Ekiben (station bento box) purchased at Tokyo Station before boarding the Shinkansen — a beloved Japanese travel tradition — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Picnic bento from Nishiki Market or a convenience store, enjoyed under the cherry blossoms in Maruyama Park — budget ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Traditional kaiseki-style set dinner (simplified, mid-range version) in Higashiyama — try Kikunoi Roan or a local tofu kaiseki restaurant — budget ¥3,500–¥5,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen tickets in advance, especially for April (peak cherry blossom season). A JR Pass covering Tokyo–Kyoto–Hiroshima–Tokyo would be excellent value for this trip — purchase before leaving home. Maruyama Park is free to enter. Kiyomizudera admission is ¥400 per adult.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Tenryu-ji Garden — Take the JR Sagano Line to Saga-Arashiyama Station (20 minutes from Kyoto Station). Arrive by 8:00–8:30 AM to experience the bamboo grove before crowds arrive. Walk the famous path through towering green bamboo stalks — an otherworldly, meditative experience. Then enter Tenryu-ji, a UNESCO World Heritage Zen temple with one of Japan's finest garden designs featuring a pond reflecting the Arashiyama mountains — a masterpiece of borrowed scenery (shakkei).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Arashiyama: rent a bicycle or take a rickshaw ride along the Oi River (Hozu River) with mountain views. Visit the Okochi Sanso Villa garden for panoramic views over Kyoto. Walk through the charming Saga-Toriimoto preserved historic street. Consider a short boat ride on the Hozu River if time allows (1.5-hour scenic gorge boat ride, book in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto. Visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's famous 'kitchen' — a narrow five-block covered arcade with over 100 food stalls and shops selling pickles, fresh tofu, grilled skewers, and Kyoto specialties. Perfect for grazing and souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a matcha-themed café near Arashiyama — try % Arabica Arashiyama for a world-class coffee with bamboo grove views — budget ¥600–¥900
meals.lunch: Yudofu (hot tofu) set lunch at a restaurant near Tenryu-ji — a Kyoto specialty perfectly suited to the Arashiyama temple district — budget ¥1,500–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Pontocho Alley dinner — Kyoto's most atmospheric dining lane along the Kamo River. Choose from dozens of restaurants offering everything from yakitori to French-Japanese fusion. Riverside terrace (kawayuka) dining in spring is magical — budget ¥3,000–¥4,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tenryu-ji garden admission is ¥500 (garden only) or ¥800 (including temple building). Okochi Sanso Villa is ¥1,000 and includes a bowl of matcha tea — excellent value. The bamboo grove path is free. Go early to avoid tour groups. Arashiyama is very popular — weekday mornings are significantly less crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — Take the JR Nara Line to Inari Station (5 minutes from Kyoto Station). Hike through the iconic tunnel of thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up Mount Inari. The full hike to the summit and back takes 2–3 hours, but even going 45 minutes up to Yotsutsuji intersection offers spectacular views over Kyoto. This is one of Japan's most visually stunning and spiritually significant Shinto shrines — free to enter and open 24/7.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Nara for an afternoon day trip (45 minutes from Kyoto by JR Miyakoji Rapid). Visit Nara Park, home to over 1,000 freely roaming sacred deer that bow for shika senbei (deer crackers, sold for ¥200). Walk to Todai-ji Temple housing the world's largest bronze Buddha statue (Daibutsu). Explore the surrounding Kasuga Taisha Shrine with its hundreds of stone and bronze lanterns.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the Gion district, Kyoto's famous geisha quarter. Stroll Hanamikoji Street at dusk for a chance to spot a geiko or maiko (Kyoto geisha) heading to evening engagements.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near Fushimi Inari — inari sushi (fried tofu pouches filled with rice, named after the shrine's fox deity) from a local shop — budget ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Nara kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf-wrapped sushi) bento or a casual restaurant near Nara Park — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Gion district restaurant — try obanzai (Kyoto-style home cooking with small seasonal dishes) at a mid-range restaurant — budget ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free and the most-visited site in Kyoto — go early (before 8 AM) or late to avoid peak crowds. Todai-ji admission is ¥600 per adult, ¥300 for children. Nara Park is free. Buy deer crackers from official vendors only. Gion strolling is free — be respectful of geiko/maiko privacy and do not block their path for photos.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Kyoto to Hiroshima via Shinkansen — Take the Shinkansen Nozomi or Hikari from Kyoto Station to Hiroshima (approximately 1 hour). Check into Hiroshima accommodation or store luggage. Proceed directly to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — this UNESCO World Heritage Site is the emotional and historical heart of the trip. The museum chronicles the atomic bombing of August 6, 1945, through personal testimonies, artifacts, and photographs. Allow 1.5–2 hours for a thorough, respectful visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in the Peace Memorial Park — walk through the park grounds, visit the A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), the Children's Peace Monument (inspired by Sadako Sasaki), and the Flame of Peace. Take a moment of quiet reflection at the Memorial Cenotaph. Then take the Hiroshima Electric Railway (streetcar) or ferry to Miyajima Island (Itsukushima) — famous for its 'floating' torii gate rising from the sea. Explore Itsukushima Shrine and interact with the island's friendly deer.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima city for dinner. Explore the Hondori covered shopping arcade and the lively Nagarekawa entertainment district.

meals.breakfast: Shinkansen ekiben or hotel breakfast before departing Kyoto
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory pancake layered with noodles, cabbage, pork, and egg — completely different from Osaka-style) at Okonomimura, a multi-floor building housing dozens of okonomiyaki restaurants — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Hiroshima oysters — the city is famous for its plump, briny oysters. Try them grilled (kaki no dote nabe), fried (kaki furai), or raw at a restaurant near the Peace Park or Nagarekawa — budget ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Peace Memorial Museum admission is ¥200 per adult — one of the most important and moving museums in the world. Allow adequate time and emotional space. The museum is appropriate for older children (10+) but may be intense for younger children. Miyajima ferry is ¥180 each way (JR Pass holders ride free on JR Ferry). Itsukushima Shrine admission is ¥300. Check tide times — the floating torii is most dramatic at high tide.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Miyajima Island for a deeper morning exploration — the island is far more peaceful in the early morning before day-trippers arrive. Hike up Mount Misen (535m) via the ropeway (¥1,000 one-way, ¥1,840 return) for panoramic views of the Seto Inland Sea and its 700 islands. The primeval forest on the mountain is a UNESCO-listed sacred natural site. Visit the Misen Main Hall and the eternal flame said to have been burning for 1,200 years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hiroshima and travel back toward the Kansai/Tokyo area. Take the Shinkansen from Hiroshima to Osaka (approximately 1 hour 20 minutes). Check into Osaka accommodation. Explore Dotonbori — Osaka's neon-lit entertainment and food district along the canal, famous for its giant crab and Glico running man signs. This is the heart of Osaka's 'kuidaore' (eat until you drop) culture.
day_by_day.evening: Full Dotonbori and Namba evening experience — take a canal boat cruise (¥900 per person) for a unique perspective on the illuminated signs, then explore the surrounding Shinsaibashi shopping arcade and Amerika-Mura (American Village) for street culture.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast on Miyajima Island — try momiji manju (maple leaf-shaped cakes filled with sweet red bean paste), the island's iconic souvenir snack — budget ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at Hiroshima Station before boarding Shinkansen — another round of Hiroshima okonomiyaki or a bento box
meals.dinner: Dotonbori food crawl — takoyaki (octopus balls) from Wanaka or Aizuya, kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) from Daruma, and finish with soft-serve matcha ice cream — budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person for a full grazing dinner

day_by_day.notes: Mount Misen ropeway operates from approximately 9:00 AM. The hike from the ropeway exit to the summit takes 30 minutes each way — wear good shoes. Osaka is only 15 minutes from Shin-Osaka Station to Namba by subway (¥290). Dotonbori is extremely crowded on Friday evenings — keep belongings secure and enjoy the vibrant chaos.

day_by_day.morning: Osaka Castle and Nishinomaru Garden — Visit Osaka Castle, one of Japan's most iconic landmarks and a symbol of the nation's feudal history. The surrounding Nishinomaru Garden (¥200 admission) is one of Osaka's best cherry blossom spots — late-blooming varieties may still be flowering in late April. Climb to the top floor of the castle tower (¥600 admission) for panoramic city views and explore the excellent historical museum inside covering Toyotomi Hideyoshi's era.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kuromon Ichiba Market ('Osaka's Kitchen') — Visit this 580-stall covered market for a final immersive Japanese food experience. Sample fresh uni (sea urchin), wagyu beef skewers, fresh crab, and seasonal produce. Then visit Shinsekai district — a retro 1920s-themed neighborhood with Tsutenkaku Tower and the birthplace of kushikatsu. This nostalgic, slightly gritty area offers a completely different side of Osaka.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Japan — Return to Dotonbori or Namba for a farewell dinner. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Don Quijote (open until midnight) or the Shinsaibashi-suji covered arcade. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Japan's history, culture, and natural beauty.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Japanese breakfast set (gohan, miso shiru, grilled salmon, pickles, tamagoyaki) at a local diner near the hotel — budget ¥800–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Kuromon Market grazing lunch — fresh seafood, grilled items, and Japanese street food — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range Japanese restaurant in Namba — try a full teppanyaki experience or a high-quality sushi counter for a memorable final meal — budget ¥4,000–¥6,000 per person as a special treat

day_by_day.notes: Osaka Castle is open 9:00 AM–5:00 PM. The surrounding park and moat area are free. Pack any purchased Japanese knives, ceramics, or food items carefully for the flight home. If departing from Kansai International Airport (KIX), allow 60–90 minutes travel time from Namba via the Nankai Rapi:t express (¥1,430, 38 minutes). If departing from Tokyo, catch an early Shinkansen the next morning. Japan requires you to declare all food items at customs — check what is permitted to bring back to your home country.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy traditional sakura mochi and bento boxes, and soak in the festive atmosphere with locals and families. The illuminated evening viewing is especially breathtaking.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Walk the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional craft stalls and street food vendors. Kids will love trying ningyo-yaki (doll-shaped cakes) and watching artisans at work. A perfect blend of history and family fun.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and educational experience for families, this UNESCO World Heritage site tells the story of the 1945 atomic bombing through powerful exhibits and preserved ruins. The Peace Park surrounding the museum offers reflective walks along the river and the iconic Atomic Bomb Dome. Essential for understanding modern Japanese history.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Tenryu-ji Garden
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic natural and cultural landscapes. Combine the visit with the UNESCO-listed Tenryu-ji Zen garden featuring stunning cherry blossom trees reflected in its central pond. Rent a rickshaw for a family-friendly tour of the surrounding historic village.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japanese culinary culture at the world-famous Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), wagyu beef skewers, and matcha-flavored treats from dozens of stalls. Join a guided family-friendly food tour to learn about Japanese food traditions, seasonal ingredients, and the art of sushi-making from local vendors.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront property to acclimate and decompress from the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle introduction to Japanese cuisine with a private kaiseki dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Enjoy a curated multi-course meal featuring seasonal spring ingredients, paired with premium sake selections chosen by the in-house sommelier.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport dining before arrival
meals.lunch: N/A — arriving at 13:00; light welcome refreshments provided at resort check-in
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — multi-course seasonal tasting menu with sake pairing (approx. ¥25,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day is intentionally light. Jet lag management is key — avoid overscheduling. Request the resort's butler service to pre-stock your room with preferred beverages and snacks. Confirm all upcoming reservations with the concierge this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a lavish breakfast at the resort before departing for Tokyo. Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Arrive early to experience the serene atmosphere before crowds peak. Walk the historic Nakamise Shopping Street, browsing traditional crafts, folding fans, and wagashi (Japanese sweets) from artisan vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the broader Asakusa district on foot with a private cultural guide. Visit Asakusa Shrine, try on a kimono at a premium rental studio, and take a rickshaw (jinrikisha) ride through the historic backstreets for a truly immersive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the upscale Ginza district for dinner. Dine at a Michelin-starred tempura or sushi restaurant. After dinner, enjoy a cocktail at a rooftop bar with panoramic Tokyo skyline views.

meals.breakfast: Premium buffet or à la carte breakfast at the resort — fresh pastries, Japanese and Western options, freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Traditional soba lunch at a renowned noodle house in Asakusa (e.g., Kanda Yabu Soba style) — approx. ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred restaurant in Ginza (e.g., tempura omakase or premium sushi counter) — approx. ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ginza restaurant reservation well in advance — Michelin-starred seats fill up months ahead. Arrange a private English-speaking guide for the Asakusa morning tour for the richest cultural context. Dress modestly for temple visits.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Tsukiji Outer Market for a guided premium food tour. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and seasonal Japanese street foods. Learn about Japan's legendary fish culture and culinary philosophy from a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to the Imperial Palace East Gardens for a peaceful walk through manicured traditional gardens. Afterward, visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum (or Tokyo National Museum in Ueno) to explore Japan's rich samurai and shogunate history through world-class exhibits — ideal for culture and history enthusiasts of all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a traditional robatayaki restaurant in the Marunouchi or Nihonbashi district — charcoal-grilled seasonal fish, wagyu beef, and vegetables prepared tableside by skilled chefs. End the evening with a stroll along the illuminated Imperial Palace moat.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before departure, or grab fresh items at Tsukiji Outer Market as part of the food tour
meals.lunch: Omakase sushi lunch at a top-tier counter near Tsukiji — approx. ¥15,000–¥25,000 per person
meals.dinner: Premium robatayaki dinner in Marunouchi — approx. ¥20,000–¥30,000 per person with craft beer or sake pairings

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji food tour is best started by 8:00–9:00 AM for the freshest selections. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Edo-Tokyo Museum is very family-friendly with interactive exhibits and English audio guides available.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer (Shinkansen Green Car or private charter) from Tokyo to Kyoto — approximately 2.5 hours. Check in to a premium Kyoto ryokan or luxury hotel. After settling in, head to Arashiyama for a morning walk through the ethereal Bamboo Grove — a UNESCO-recognized cultural landscape. The filtered morning light through the towering bamboo is truly magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Tenryu-ji Garden adjacent to the Bamboo Grove — a masterpiece of Zen garden design with a stunning pond reflecting the Arashiyama mountains. Enjoy a traditional shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian) lunch at the garden's in-house restaurant. Afterward, take a private boat ride along the Oi River for a serene perspective of the Arashiyama landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto city center. Enjoy a private tea ceremony experience at a historic machiya (townhouse) in Gion. Dinner at a kaiseki restaurant in Gion overlooking a traditional garden.

meals.breakfast: Bento breakfast box in the Shinkansen Green Car, or light meal at Tokyo Station's premium food hall (Gransta)
meals.lunch: Shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) at Tenryu-ji's Shigetsu restaurant — approx. ¥6,000–¥10,000 per person
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner in Gion — approx. ¥30,000–¥45,000 per person with seasonal sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Shinkansen Green Car seats in advance. Arashiyama is most peaceful on weekday mornings — a Sunday visit may be busier, so aim for an early start (by 8:30 AM). Confirm ryokan check-in time to ensure seamless arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Iconic cherry blossom viewing (hanami) at Maruyama Park — home to Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura). Mid-April is peak bloom season. Arrive early morning for a peaceful picnic-style hanami breakfast under the blossoms. Your concierge can arrange a premium picnic hamper with champagne, matcha, and artisan Japanese snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the nearby Higashiyama district — a beautifully preserved historic neighborhood with stone-paved lanes, traditional craft shops, and ancient shrines. Visit Yasaka Shrine and Chion-in Temple. Stop at a premium wagashi (Japanese confectionery) atelier for a private sweet-making demonstration.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi) — a canal-side walkway lined with hundreds of cherry trees in full bloom, absolutely breathtaking at dusk. Dinner at a Michelin-starred restaurant in central Kyoto.

meals.breakfast: Premium hanami picnic hamper arranged by concierge — champagne, seasonal Japanese bites, matcha, artisan sweets under the cherry blossoms
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a traditional ochazuke or tofu kaiseki restaurant in Higashiyama — approx. ¥5,000–¥8,000 per person
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred Kyoto cuisine (kyo-ryori) — approx. ¥35,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Cherry blossom peak in mid-April can vary by year — confirm bloom forecasts closer to the date. The Philosopher's Path at sunset is a highlight not to be missed. Wear comfortable shoes for extensive walking on cobblestones in Higashiyama.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Fushimi Inari Taisha — the iconic shrine famous for thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up the mountain. An early morning visit (before 8:00 AM) ensures a mystical, crowd-free experience. Hike to the upper shrine for panoramic views over Kyoto.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nijo Castle — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and former residence of the Tokugawa shoguns. Explore its famous 'nightingale floors' and stunning painted screen rooms with a private historian guide. Afterward, browse Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') for artisan pickles, premium teas, and local specialties.
day_by_day.evening: Private geisha dinner experience (ozashiki) in Gion — an exclusive and rare cultural experience where a maiko or geiko entertains guests with traditional dance, music, and conversation. One of Japan's most coveted luxury cultural experiences.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the ryokan before the Fushimi Inari visit
meals.lunch: Premium bento lunch or kaiseki-style lunch at a Fushimi-area restaurant — approx. ¥8,000–¥12,000 per person
meals.dinner: Ozashiki geisha dinner in Gion — multi-course kaiseki with geiko/maiko entertainment — approx. ¥60,000–¥100,000 per person (must be booked months in advance through a trusted concierge)

day_by_day.notes: The ozashiki geisha dinner is the crown jewel of a luxury Kyoto experience and requires advance booking through a specialized concierge or cultural liaison — this is not available to walk-in guests. Confirm arrangements before the trip begins.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hiroshima via Shinkansen (approximately 1 hour from Kyoto). Begin at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — a profoundly moving UNESCO World Heritage site. Visit the A-Bomb Dome, Peace Bell, and Children's Peace Monument with a knowledgeable guide who provides historical context in a thoughtful, family-appropriate manner.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry to Miyajima Island — one of Japan's most scenic locations. Visit the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine at high tide. Stroll the island's forested paths and interact with the friendly resident deer. Try Hiroshima-style oysters and momiji manju (maple leaf cakes) from local vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by Shinkansen. Wind down with a relaxing in-room kaiseki dinner or private onsen bath at the ryokan, reflecting on the day's emotional and cultural depth.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan breakfast before departure — traditional Japanese morning meal with grilled fish, rice, miso soup, and pickles
meals.lunch: Premium Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki lunch at a celebrated local restaurant — approx. ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person
meals.dinner: In-room kaiseki dinner at the ryokan or a quiet Kyoto restaurant — approx. ¥20,000–¥30,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is deeply emotional — prepare children in an age-appropriate way beforehand. The museum is educational and handled with great sensitivity. Allow at least 2 hours at the museum and 2–3 hours on Miyajima Island. Check Shinkansen schedules in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Kyoto — enjoy the ryokan's onsen facilities, a meditation session, or a private ikebana (flower arranging) or calligraphy class arranged by the concierge. A gentle, restorative morning after the emotionally rich Hiroshima day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kinkaku-ji (the Golden Pavilion) — one of Japan's most iconic and photographed landmarks, especially beautiful surrounded by spring foliage and cherry blossoms. Continue to Ryoan-ji Temple to contemplate its world-famous Zen rock garden. End with a visit to Ninna-ji Temple's cherry blossom garden — a lesser-known but stunning bloom spot.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Kyoto at an exclusive teppanyaki restaurant featuring A5 Wagyu beef from Kobe or Kyoto Nishiki beef, prepared tableside by a master chef. Celebrate the journey so far with a premium Japanese whisky tasting from a curated selection.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely ryokan breakfast — traditional multi-dish Japanese morning spread
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a temple-adjacent tea house — matcha, wagashi, and light seasonal dishes — approx. ¥4,000–¥6,000 per person
meals.dinner: Premium teppanyaki A5 Wagyu dinner with Japanese whisky tasting — approx. ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Kinkaku-ji can be crowded in the afternoon — consider visiting just after opening (9:00 AM) if the morning leisure is shortened. The Japanese whisky tasting can be arranged at the restaurant or at a specialist whisky bar in Kyoto's Gion district.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer back to the Tokyo area or onward to the resort. En route, stop at Hakone for a scenic detour — take the Hakone Ropeway over volcanic Mount Hakone with views of Mount Fuji (weather permitting). Visit the open-air Hakone Open-Air Museum, a world-class sculpture park ideal for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy an afternoon of relaxation — take advantage of the beachfront, spa treatments, or a private sunset sailing excursion arranged by the resort. A restorative afternoon before the final full day.
day_by_day.evening: Beachside private dining experience arranged by the resort — a curated seafood feast featuring premium Japanese seafood (uni, lobster, abalone) prepared by the resort's executive chef, with a bonfire and champagne under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan breakfast before checkout
meals.lunch: Casual but premium lunch at a Hakone restaurant or resort café — fresh mountain cuisine, soba, or seasonal dishes — approx. ¥5,000–¥8,000 per person
meals.dinner: Private beachside seafood dinner at the resort — approx. ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person with champagne and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Mount Fuji visibility is weather-dependent — have a backup plan if clouds obscure the view. The Hakone Open-Air Museum is one of Japan's best family-friendly cultural attractions. Confirm the private beachside dinner setup with the resort concierge at least 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a leisurely breakfast with ocean views. Take one last walk along the beachfront, swim, or indulge in a farewell spa treatment (hot stone massage or traditional Japanese shiatsu). Pack souvenirs purchased throughout the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final light lunch at the resort. Private luxury transfer to the airport with ample time for check-in. Browse duty-free for premium Japanese gifts — matcha, sake, wagashi, and cosmetics.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 10 extraordinary days of cherry blossoms, ancient temples, world-class cuisine, and unforgettable cultural immersion across Japan.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full spread of Japanese and Western options, fresh juices, premium coffee and teas
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or airport premium lounge — seasonal Japanese bento or à la carte
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport procedures. Ask the concierge to arrange airport lounge access for a comfortable pre-departure experience. Consider purchasing a curated gift box of premium Japanese goods from the resort's boutique as a lasting memento.
